title: Farm Machines and Tools
hint: Tractor, plough, combine, baler; spade, rake, hoe, pitchfork; used to, used for, so that, in order to
why: farm machines are big, loud and everywhere in the countryside, and garden tools are in almost every home. Knowing their names, and how to say what something is used for, helps you describe any tool or machine, on a farm or in your own garden.
know: is used to, is used for, in order to, so that
able: name common farm machines and garden tools
explain what a machine or tool does and what it is used for
say why people do things: She bought a quad bike to check the fences.
mistakes: A spade is used for dig.
A spade is used for digging. / A spade is used to dig.
I came here for learn about farms.
I came here to learn about farms.
He wears gloves for to protect his hands.
He wears gloves to protect his hands.
The machine for harvest wheat is a combine.
The machine for harvesting wheat is a combine.
We cover the hay so that it stay dry.
We cover the hay so that it stays dry.
Pass me the shears, please. (always plural, like scissors)
warmup: Which farm machines can you name in English? Have you ever sat on a tractor?
Do you have a garden or a balcony with plants? Which tools do you use?
Think of one tool in your kitchen. What is it for? Try to explain it without saying its name.

rows: tractor
a strong vehicle that pulls other machines and trailers
trailer
a cart pulled behind a tractor; it carries hay, crops or animals
plough (US/Canada plow)
turns over the soil before planting
harrow
breaks the soil into small pieces after ploughing
seed drill
puts seeds into the ground in neat rows
sprayer
sprays water, fertiliser or chemicals on crops
combine harvester (a combine)
cuts grain crops and separates the grain from the straw
baler
presses hay or straw into bales (big round or square blocks)
quad bike (US/Canada ATV)
a small motorbike with four wheels for getting around the farm
spade
a flat, sharp blade on a handle, for digging
shovel
a wide, curved blade, for moving soil, sand or snow
pitchfork
a long fork, for lifting hay and straw
hoe
a thin, flat blade on a long handle, for removing weeds
rake
a row of metal or plastic teeth, for collecting leaves and making soil smooth
wheelbarrow
a small cart with one wheel, for carrying soil, stones or manure
shears
very big scissors, for cutting hedges or sheep's wool (always plural)
bucket
a round container with a handle, for carrying water or feed
is used to + verb
the job of a tool or machine
A harrow is used to break up the soil.
is used for + -ing / noun
the same idea, with -ing or a noun
A pitchfork is used for lifting hay. This trailer is for animals.
to + verb
why someone does something
She bought a quad bike to check the fences.
in order to + verb
the same, more formal
Farmers rotate crops in order to keep the soil healthy.
so that + subject + verb
the result you want; often with can or will
We cover the hay so that it stays dry.

say: plough rhymes with cow; a COMbine (the machine) has stress on the first part, but to comBINE (mix) has stress on the second; hoe sounds like go; SHOvel rhymes with love-l; shears rhymes with ears.

exercises.title: What does it do?
exercises.intro: Match each machine or tool to its job. Tap one, then tap what it does.

items.why: A tractor is the farm's strongest vehicle. It pulls other machines, like a plough or a trailer.
A plough (US/Canada plow) turns over the soil before farmers plant seeds.

items.r: breaks the soil into small pieces
items.why: A harrow comes after the plough. It breaks big pieces of soil into small ones.

items.r: puts seeds into the ground in rows
items.why: A seed drill makes small holes and puts seeds into the ground in neat rows.

items.r: sprays crops with water or chemicals
items.why: A sprayer sprays water, fertiliser or chemicals onto crops.

items.r: cuts grain and separates it from the straw
items.why: A combine harvester cuts wheat or barley and separates the grain from the straw at the same time.
A baler presses hay or straw into bales: big round or square blocks.

items.r: carries soil or manure by hand
items.why: A wheelbarrow is a small cart with one wheel. You push it to carry soil, stones or manure.
is used to + verb: used to remove weeds. (Or: used for removing weeds.)
After for, use -ing: used for collecting leaves.

items.pre: The farmer bought a quad bike

items.why: To say why someone does something, use to + verb: to check the sheep. Not for or for to.

is for + -ing: This trailer is for carrying animals.

use something + to + verb: use shears to cut the wool.

exercises.title: Reading
exercises.text:
Green Valley Farm: Open Day
Saturday 14 September, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Come and see how a modern farm works! This year our theme is farm machines, old and new.

In the big barn you can sit in the cab of our new tractor. It has air conditioning and a computer screen, and it uses GPS so that it can drive in perfectly straight lines. Next to it is our combine harvester, which is used for harvesting wheat and barley. It is as tall as a house!

In the yard, our neighbour Frank will show you his collection of old machines. His oldest plough is more than a hundred years old. In those days, horses were used to pull it.

Children can try our hand tools in the vegetable garden: they can dig with a spade, collect leaves with a rake and have a wheelbarrow race. At 2 p.m. there is a tractor-and-trailer ride around the farm.

Tickets cost $10 for adults. Children under twelve are free. Please wear old shoes, because the farmyard can be muddy!
exercises.intro: Read the leaflet. Then type the missing word from the text, and press Check.

items.ask: What can you sit in, in the big barn?
items.why: Paragraph 3: 'In the big barn you can sit in the cab of our new tractor.'

items.pre: So that it can drive in perfectly straight
items.why: Paragraph 3: 'it uses GPS so that it can drive in perfectly straight lines'.

items.ask: What is the combine harvester used for?
items.why: Paragraph 3: 'used for harvesting wheat and barley'.
Paragraph 4: 'In those days, horses were used to pull it.'

items.why: Paragraph 6: 'wear old shoes, because the farmyard can be muddy'.

exercises.title: Speaking
items: Choose a tool from your kitchen, garden or toolbox. Describe it without saying its name: It's used for ... It's made of ... Can your teacher guess it?
How have farm machines changed since your grandparents' time? Do you know anyone who still works by hand or with animals?
Would you like to drive a tractor or a combine harvester? Why or why not?
Self-driving tractors and drones are now used on some farms. What do you think they are used for? Is this a good thing?

parts.rule:
Watch out

  • used to + verb: A spade is used to dig holes.
  • used for + -ing: A spade is used for digging holes.
  • Both are correct and mean the same. Never used for dig or used to digging (for a tool's job).
parts.intro: Which phrase goes with each ending? Sort them.

chips.why: Base verb after used to: used to dig holes.
-ing after used for: used for digging holes.
Base verb after used to: used to carry soil.
-ing after used for: used for carrying soil.
Base verb after used to: used to collect leaves.
-ing after used for: used for collecting leaves.
Base verb after used to: used to lift hay.
-ing after used for: used for lifting hay.
Base verb after used to: used to remove weeds.
-ing after used for: used for removing weeds.

items.q: A spade is used for dig holes.
items.why: After for, use -ing: used for digging holes. (Or: used to dig holes.)

items.q: He bought a trailer for carry the bales.
items.why: To say why, use to + verb: He bought a trailer to carry the bales.

items.q: We covered the hay so that it stays dry.
items.why: Correct: so that + subject + verb: so that it stays dry.

items.q: The sprayer is used to protecting the crops.
items.why: is used to + base verb: used to protect the crops.

items.q: Farmers use a combine for to harvest wheat.
items.why: Never for to. Say: Farmers use a combine to harvest wheat.

teacher.purpose: give general learners the names of common farm machines and hand tools (tractor, plough, combine harvester, baler; spade, rake, hoe, pitchfork, wheelbarrow) and the language of purpose: is used to + verb, is used for + -ing, to, in order to and so that. The reading is a farm open-day leaflet.
teacher.before: find photos of three or four farm machines (a tractor, a combine, a baler) and a few garden tools; a garden centre website or a toy catalogue works well. Ask the student to have one tool from home ready to show on camera.
plan: The three warm-up questions. The third (describe a kitchen tool without its name) shows you how the student already talks about purpose.
Machines first, in the order of the farming year: plough, harrow, seed drill, sprayer, combine, baler. Then the hand tools, ideally with real objects or photos. Then the purpose phrases.
Matching, then the purpose phrases. In Exercise 2, ask the student to say each sentence a second way: used to remove → used for removing.
Do one together and set the other for home.
The open-day leaflet. First ask: “Would you go? What would you most like to see?” Then the questions. Point out so that it can drive and horses were used to pull it.
Question 1 (the guessing game) is the core and good fun: take turns. Then Question 2 or 4.
Exercise 7 Part A together; Part B at home.
pron: plough /plaʊ/: rhymes with cow. The -ough spelling confuses everyone (though, through, tough); the US/Canada spelling plow shows the sound.
combine: the machine is /ˈkɒmbaɪn/ (stress first), the verb to combine is /kəmˈbaɪn/ (stress second).
mistakes: for + verb: Spanish para, French pour, Italian per, Portuguese para + infinitive lead to I came for learn or for to learn. In English, purpose is to + verb; for takes a noun or -ing (for digging, for hay).
is used to + verb (a tool's job) vs be used to + -ing (accustomed): A hoe is used to remove weeds vs I'm used to getting up early. Mention it only if the student mixes them.
so that needs a subject and verb: so that it stays dry, so that we can finish. In order to and to need just a verb.
spade vs shovel: a spade digs (flat, sharp edge); a shovel moves loose things (wide, curved). In everyday North American English, people often say shovel for both.
machinery, equipment are uncountable: farm machinery, new equipment. Not machineries or an equipment. Say a machine or a piece of equipment.
shears (and scissors) are always plural: these shears are sharp, a pair of shears.
uk_us: Canadian spelling varies; both are used.
In the UK too, farmers usually just say the combine.
A hayride in North America is a ride on a hay wagon.
Canadian spelling often follows the US here.
adapt: Focus on tractor, trailer, plough, combine, and spade, shovel, rake, wheelbarrow, bucket. Phrases: used to + verb, used for + -ing, to + verb.
All words; add cultivator, mower, irrigation system, drone, auger, and so as to, with the aim of, which allows farmers to.
The guessing game with everyday tools; say what three tools at home are used for.
Explain a modern machine (a milking robot, a drone) to someone who has never seen one, or discuss whether technology is good for small farms.
prompts: Guess the tool. Take turns. Follow up with questions: “Is it made of metal?” “Do you use it outside?” “What else is it used for?” Listen for used for + verb.
Machines then and now. Follow up: “What did farmers use before tractors?” (horses, oxen) “What jobs did people do by hand?” Good for were used to pull.
Drive a tractor or a combine? Follow up: “What do you think is the hardest part?” “Why do farmers sometimes work all night at harvest time?” (to finish before the rain)
Self-driving tractors and drones. Follow up: “What are drones used for on a farm?” (checking crops, spraying, finding lost sheep) “Who wins and who loses?”

bank.q: A ___ is used for lifting hay and straw.
bank.why: A pitchfork is a long fork for lifting hay and straw. A hoe removes weeds, and a spade digs.

bank.q: The ___ cuts the wheat and separates the grain from the straw.
bank.why: A combine harvester cuts grain crops and separates the grain from the straw.

bank.q: My aunt uses a hoe ___ the weeds between her carrots.
bank.why: use something + to + verb: uses a hoe to remove the weeds.

bank.q: This machine is used for ___ seeds in straight rows.
bank.why: After for, use -ing: used for planting seeds.

bank.q: We got up at five ___ we could finish before the heat.
bank.why: Before a subject and verb (we could finish), use so that.

bank.q: He rode the quad bike up the hill ___ check the fences.
bank.why: To say why, use to + verb: to check the fences.

bank.q: Farmers spend a lot of money on ___.
bank.why: Machinery is uncountable: no -s and no a. For one, say a machine.

bank.q: You'll need a ___ to move all those bricks.
bank.why: A wheelbarrow is a small cart with one wheel for carrying heavy things like bricks or soil.

bank.q: In Canada you can plow a field; in Britain you ___ it.
bank.why: The British spelling is plough. It sounds the same as plow and rhymes with cow.

bank.q: My neighbour checks his cows on a ___ every morning.
bank.why: A quad bike (US/Canada ATV) is a small four-wheeled motorbike for getting around a farm.

bank.q: Use the ___ to collect all the leaves into a pile.
bank.why: A rake has a row of teeth for collecting leaves and making soil smooth.

bank.q: The ___ presses the straw into big round bales.
bank.why: A baler presses hay or straw into bales.

bank.q: We left early in ___ to avoid the traffic.
bank.why: in order to + verb is a more formal way to say to: in order to avoid the traffic.

bank.q: This tool is used for cut hedges.
bank.why: After for, use -ing: used for cutting hedges. (Or: used to cut hedges.)

bank.q: She bought new shears for to cut the wool.
bank.why: Never for to. To say why, use to + verb: She bought new shears to cut the wool.

bank.q: We put the tools in the shed so that they don't get wet.
bank.why: Correct: so that + subject + verb: so that they don't get wet.

bank.q: The farmer needs a new equipments for the dairy.
bank.why: Equipment is uncountable: no a and no -s. Say new equipment.

bank.a: What do farmers use a harrow for?
bank.why: Question about purpose: What do + subject + use + thing + for? For goes at the end.

bank.a: The tractor is pulling a trailer full of hay.
bank.why: Subject + is + -ing + object: The tractor is pulling a trailer full of hay.

bank.a: She uses a spade to plant the potatoes.
bank.why: use + tool + to + verb (the purpose): uses a spade to plant the potatoes.
